主要内容: Before the stock market opens on Thursday, April 28, investors should be aware of several key developments. Nasdaq futures are expected to rise significantly, driven by a strong performance from Meta Platforms, which reported better-than-expected earnings. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index is in a bear market, having reached its lowest point for the year. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 are set to open higher after modest gains in the previous session. The S&P 500 is still in a correction, and the Dow is close to the correction threshold. Other notable movements include Teladoc's sharp decline after an earnings miss, Southwest Airlines' rise due to an optimistic outlook, and Ford's modest gain after slightly beating earnings and revenue expectations. The U.S. economy contracted by 1.4% in the first quarter, which was slightly better than the expected 1% growth. The Federal Reserve is closely monitoring these reports to determine the appropriate interest rate hikes to combat inflation without stifling economic growth. Before the stock market opens on Thursday, April 28, several key developments are expected to impact investor sentiment. Meta Platforms is facing pressure as its stock remains down more than 40% for the year, despite a premarket rise. Twitter, which is set to report its first-quarter earnings, is also under scrutiny as its board has agreed to sell the company to Elon Musk for $44 billion. Although Twitter shares rose 1% to around $49 each, this is still below Musk's $54.20 per share cash offer. The company reported better-than-expected monetizable daily active users but slightly below revenue expectations. Meanwhile, Dow components such as McDonald's and Caterpillar are expected to see mixed reactions, with McDonald's rising due to strong revenue and Caterpillar falling despite meeting earnings and revenue targets. Merck is also set to open higher due to strong performance in its key products. Eli Lilly's obesity drug tirzepatide showed promising results in a 72-week trial, with participants losing up to 52 pounds on average, leading to a 4% rise in its shares. These developments highlight the mixed performance of major stocks ahead of the market open.
